answer: Admission starts at a working cargo wharf. Each new key checks one serialized crate and locks a 500-token bond to the weighbill. Overnight, two stevedores the applicant does not pick sign mass and seal; at a random minute after dawn a downstream clerk must find that seal intact, so a timed ripple of custody stamps moves inland without a pre-staged helper. The crate rests on a surveyed ballast dune whose mass cannot be shared: reused serials, shifts, or piles fuse the keys and burn both bonds. Fifty aliases need fifty crates and fifty distinct piles, so extra names cost more than they return.
